why: Every app the App Factory ever produced was refused by the device at the first parse,
and both halves' suites were green while it happened. Three separate reasons, one shape:
each half only ever restated its own spelling to itself.
* two templates wrote `{port}`; the device's placeholder is `<port>` and it refuses
`{` and `}` anywhere in a command as composition characters;
* the cli-tool template carried no `run` section; the device requires one;
* it carried no `port` either, and the device requires a port of a web project - so a
CLI tool, which binds nothing, had no truthful manifest it could send at all.
The last one was not only the Cloud Core's fault: `port: 0` (`binds nothing`) was the
device's own vocabulary for a 3D batch run and a web project could not use it. It can now,
and a project that declares no port is RUN as a batch - started, waited for, answered with
its exit - instead of waiting for a socket that never opens.

rules.entry: required; a relative path that names a file of the project
rules.run: required; a non-empty object of {key: command}, every command on the allowlist
rules.test: optional; the same shape and its own allowlist
rules.port: required; 0 means the project binds nothing, otherwise 1024..65535

read_by: services/api/app/appfactory/validation.py (the Cloud Core refuses anything else before sending)
